research_areas.title: Battery modelling & digital twins
research_areas.lede: Estimating internal battery conditions and designing cloud assistance that does not compromise local safety.
research_areas.question: How should estimators, reduced-order physics and higher-fidelity models cooperate under communication and safety constraints?
methods: EKF-type state estimation and residual monitoring
Risk-based event requests and correction safety gates
research_areas.boundary: The demonstrated communication result is limited to a tested PIL configuration; physical CHIL is not yet complete.

research_areas.title: Physics-informed AI & reliable ML
research_areas.lede: Making learned battery models useful beyond a successful training run.
research_areas.question: How can battery physics, monitoring and model uncertainty support reliable predictions under changing operating conditions?
methods: SOC estimation with FCN, CNN and LSTM models
Dataset registry, drift checks and model monitoring
Exploration of physics-informed cloud-level model assistance
research_areas.boundary: Cross-chemistry generalisation and field reliability have not been established by the cited repositories.

research_areas.title: Control, estimation & embedded validation
research_areas.lede: Moving from simulation and observer logic toward measured real-time behaviour.
research_areas.question: Can edge controllers retain estimation and protection under cloud outages, faults and computational limits?
methods: Safety supervision, balancing and contactor logic
Embedded-oriented PIL work and planned OPAL-RT / TI C2000 CHIL tests
research_areas.boundary: Measured physical CHIL latency, robustness margins and formal stability guarantees remain future validation work.

research_areas.title: Energy forecasting & optimization
research_areas.lede: Data-driven forecasting and operational questions for electricity and renewable systems.
research_areas.question: How can forecasting models be evaluated fairly when demand and renewable output vary across time?
methods: Load, solar and wind forecasting interests
Error metrics and held-out evaluation as methodological priorities
Optimization interests emerging from energy-systems coursework
research_areas.boundary: A validated standalone report, complete experiment settings and benchmark tables for this topic have not been approved for publication on the portfolio.

battery-digital-twin.objective: Study whether residual-, uncertainty- and risk-aware cloud requests can reduce data exchange while retaining local estimation and safety responsibility. This is a research objective, not a proven universal theorem.
battery-digital-twin.dataset: HPPC-type pulses at 25°C for equivalent-circuit identification; UDDS at 25°C for dynamic evaluation. The supplied report plots current, voltage, cell temperature and reference SOC.
battery-digital-twin.baseline: Continuous edge-to-cloud communication, normalized to 100% of its messages in the tested PIL configuration.
battery-digital-twin.measured: Communication reduced by approximately 82.8%; the event-triggered condition therefore corresponds to 17.2% of the baseline count (derived, not separately measured).
battery-digital-twin.limitations: The report does not give a public trace-level request-count table, confidence interval or experimental repetitions for this figure. The 82.8% result must not be generalized without further tests.
battery-digital-twin.replication: A replicator would need the identified four-cell ECM/thermal parameters, drive-cycle input, event-trigger settings, safety-gate thresholds, logging definition and the original execution configuration. Those files are not included with this public website.
battery-digital-twin.interpretation: Selective communication was feasible in the reported test without delegating immediate safety responsibility to cloud updates. Communication reduction alone does not establish estimator robustness or safety in all circumstances.
battery-digital-twin.model: Vₜ = OCV(SOC, T) − IR₀ − Vₚ; rᵥ(k) = Vmeasured(k) − Vpredicted(k); γₖ ∈ {0,1}. Here γₖ = 1 denotes a cloud request.
battery-digital-twin.status: Reported PIL result; physical OPAL-RT / TI C2000 closed-loop CHIL remains planned.
battery-digital-twin.source: October 2026 project report, sections 4–6, 14–16 and 23; figures 2–6.

soc-ml.objective: Compare data-driven SOC estimation methods under a common battery-data processing and evaluation workflow.
soc-ml.dataset: LG 18650HG2 battery data; original source: Kollmeyer et al. (2020), Mendeley Data, DOI 10.17632/cp3473x7xv.3.
soc-ml.baseline: FCN, CNN and LSTM model families are described as comparators in the repository README; exact split protocol and benchmark numbers need further independent review.
soc-ml.measured: The repository documents training, Optuna tuning and MSE/MAE evaluation; no best-performing model or numerical score is asserted in this public case study.
soc-ml.limitations: The README alone does not verify out-of-domain evaluation, uncertainty calibration, an embedded deployment or full benchmark reproducibility.
soc-ml.replication: Consult the linked repository for scripts and processing steps; check the data license and original Mendeley dataset conditions before reproducing results.
soc-ml.interpretation: This project demonstrates a comparative model-development workflow rather than independently verified superiority of one neural architecture.
soc-ml.model: Supervised time-series regression using FCN, CNN and LSTM neural architectures for SOC prediction; MSE and MAE are evaluation criteria.
soc-ml.status: Public GitHub implementation; results require reproduction before quantitative comparison claims.
soc-ml.source: GitHub repository README; Kollmeyer et al., Mendeley Data V3, 2020.

battery-ml-monitoring.objective: Develop monitoring tools that can detect when deployed battery-health ML models become unreliable as incoming data changes.
battery-ml-monitoring.dataset: Battery telemetry formats, adapted SP20-style inputs and battery-specific example/demo workflows described in the public repository.
battery-ml-monitoring.baseline: A formal controlled comparison against a production monitoring baseline is not documented in the reviewed README.
battery-ml-monitoring.measured: Implemented modules documented: dataset/model registration, multi-model inference, drift/performance monitoring, alerting and deployment-oriented exports. No fleet-performance percentage claimed.
battery-ml-monitoring.limitations: The repository is a production-style prototype; operational effectiveness, field deployment and predictive alert quality need independent tests.
battery-ml-monitoring.replication: The README documents installation and make targets, including bms-demo, dashboard and test. Review environment setup and datasets before relying on example outputs.
battery-ml-monitoring.interpretation: The contribution is an ML lifecycle and monitoring framework for battery use cases, rather than a measured improvement in battery safety.
battery-ml-monitoring.model: Battery dataset registry → model inference → drift and performance checks → monitoring reports / alerting / retraining workflows.
battery-ml-monitoring.status: Public GitHub implementation; production field validation not established.
battery-ml-monitoring.source: Public README of the battery ML monitoring platform (reviewed October 2026).
